concepts.name: Rate of change
concepts.statement: The rate of change of a function measures how fast its values change as its input changes; for a linear function it is constant and given by the slope, but no single number gives it for a nonlinear function.

concepts.name: Secant
concepts.statement: The secant to the function f(x) through the points (a, f(a)) and (x, f(x)) is the line passing through these points; its slope estimates the rate of change of f at a, and the estimate improves as x gets closer to a.

concepts.name: Tangent
concepts.statement: A tangent line to the graph of a function at a point (a, f(a)) is the line that secant lines through (a, f(a)) approach as they are taken through points on the function with x-values that approach a; its slope measures the rate of change of the function at a, the derivative f′(a).

concepts.name: Tangent problem
concepts.statement: The tangent problem asks how to determine the slope of a line tangent to a curve at a point; it is solved by letting x approach a in the slope of the secant line, and it led to differential calculus.

concepts.name: Differential calculus
concepts.statement: Differential calculus is the field of calculus concerned with the study of derivatives and their applications.

concepts.name: Average velocity
concepts.statement: The average velocity of an object over a time period is the change in its position divided by the length of the time period: for a position s(t), over [a, t] it is (s(t) − s(a))/(t − a), the slope of a secant line to s.

concepts.name: Limit
concepts.statement: Letting x or t approach a in an expression is called taking a limit; the limit of a function f(x) as x approaches a is the value that f(x) approaches as x approaches a.

concepts.name: Instantaneous velocity
concepts.statement: For a position function s(t), the instantaneous velocity at a time t = a is the value that the average velocities approach on intervals of the form [a, t] and [t, a] as the values of t become closer to a, provided such a value exists.

concepts.name: Area problem
concepts.statement: The area problem asks how to find the area between the graph of a function and the x-axis over an interval [a, b]; the area is approximated by the sum of the areas of thin rectangles, and as their widths approach zero the sums approach the area, a limit that underlies the definite integral.

concepts.name: Integral calculus
concepts.statement: Integral calculus is the study of integrals and their applications.

concepts.name: Multivariable calculus
concepts.statement: Multivariable calculus is the study of the calculus of functions of two or more variables, such as motion in space and the volumes of solids under surfaces.

concepts.name: Intuitive definition of the limit
concepts.statement: Let f(x) be defined at all values in an open interval containing a, with the possible exception of a itself, and let L be a real number. If all values of f(x) approach L as the values of x (≠ a) approach a, then the limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L: as x gets closer to a, f(x) gets closer and stays close to L.

concepts.name: Evaluating a limit with a table
concepts.statement: To estimate the limit of f(x) as x approaches a, make a table of functional values for x approaching a from below and from above (a ± 0.1, a ± 0.01, …); if both columns approach a common value L, the limit is L, which a graph traced near a can confirm.

concepts.name: Two important limits
concepts.statement: For a real number a and a constant c, the limit of x as x approaches a is a, and the limit of the constant c is c.

concepts.name: Existence of a limit
concepts.statement: For the limit of a function to exist at a point, the functional values must approach a single real number there; if they do not, the limit does not exist (DNE), as for sin(1/x) as x approaches 0.

concepts.name: One-sided limit
concepts.statement: A one-sided limit is a limit taken from either the left or the right: L is the limit of f(x) as x approaches a from the left if the values f(x) approach L as x < a approaches a, and from the right if they approach L as x > a approaches a.

concepts.name: Relating one-sided and two-sided limits
concepts.statement: Let f(x) be defined at all values in an open interval containing a, with the possible exception of a, and let L be a real number. Then the limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L if and only if the limits from the left and from the right are both L.

forms.latex: \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L\;\text{if and only if}\;\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)=L\;\text{and}\;\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)=L

concepts.name: Infinite limit
concepts.statement: A function has an infinite limit at a point a if its values increase or decrease without bound as x approaches a, from the left, from the right or from both sides; writing that the limit is +∞ or −∞ describes this behavior and does not assert that a limit exists.

concepts.name: Infinite limits from positive integers
concepts.statement: For a positive integer n, 1/(x − a)ⁿ has an infinite limit at a: +∞ from both sides if n is even; +∞ from the right and −∞ from the left if n is odd.

concepts.name: Vertical asymptote
concepts.statement: The line x = a is a vertical asymptote of f(x) if the limit of f(x) as x approaches a from the left, from the right or from both sides is +∞ or −∞.

concepts.name: Sum law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits: L + M.

concepts.name: Difference law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of a difference is the difference of the limits: L − M.

concepts.name: Constant multiple law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of a constant c times a function is c times its limit: cL.

concepts.name: Product law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of a product is the product of the limits: L · M.

concepts.name: Quotient law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of a quotient is the quotient of the limits, L/M, provided M ≠ 0.

concepts.name: Power law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of the nth power of a function is the nth power of its limit, Lⁿ, for every positive integer n.

concepts.name: Root law for limits
concepts.statement: Where the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are L and M. The limit of the nth root of a function is the nth root of its limit, for all L if n is odd and for L ≥ 0 if n is even and f(x) ≥ 0.

concepts.name: Limit laws
concepts.statement: The limit laws are the individual properties of limits: for f(x) and g(x) defined for all x ≠ a over some open interval containing a, with limits L and M at a, and a constant c, the limit of a sum, difference, constant multiple, product, quotient (M ≠ 0), power or root is that combination of L and M.

concepts.name: Limits of polynomial and rational functions
concepts.statement: For polynomials p(x) and q(x) and a real number a, the limit of p(x) as x approaches a is p(a), and the limit of p(x)/q(x) is p(a)/q(a) when q(a) ≠ 0: such limits are found by direct substitution.

concepts.name: Limits of functions equal near a
concepts.statement: If f(x) = g(x) for all x ≠ a over some open interval containing a, then the limits of f(x) and g(x) as x approaches a are equal.

concepts.name: Indeterminate form 0/0
concepts.statement: A limit of f(x)/g(x) as x approaches a where the limits of f(x) and g(x) are both 0 has the indeterminate form 0/0: substitution gives no value, and the limit may still exist.

concepts.name: Evaluating a 0/0 limit
concepts.statement: To evaluate a limit of f(x)/g(x) with the indeterminate form 0/0, find a function equal to it for all x ≠ a near a, by factoring and canceling, multiplying by a conjugate where a square root is involved, or simplifying a complex fraction, then apply the limit laws.

concepts.name: Squeeze theorem
concepts.statement: Let f(x), g(x) and h(x) be defined for all x ≠ a over an open interval containing a. If f(x) ≤ g(x) ≤ h(x) for all x ≠ a in that interval and the limits of f(x) and h(x) as x approaches a are both the real number L, then the limit of g(x) is L.

concepts.name: Important trigonometric limits
concepts.statement: As θ approaches 0, sin θ approaches 0, cos θ approaches 1, sin θ/θ approaches 1 and (1 − cos θ)/θ approaches 0; the squeeze theorem on the unit circle, where sin θ < θ < tan θ for 0 < θ < π/2, establishes them.

concepts.name: Continuity at a point
concepts.statement: A function f(x) is continuous at a point a if and only if f(a) is defined, the limit of f(x) as x approaches a exists, and that limit equals f(a); intuitively, its graph has no break at a.

concepts.name: Discontinuity at a point
concepts.statement: A function is discontinuous at a point, or has a discontinuity at the point, if it is not continuous there.

concepts.name: Determining continuity at a point
concepts.statement: To decide whether f is continuous at a: check that f(a) is defined; compute the limit of f(x) as x approaches a, through the one-sided limits if needed, and check that it exists; compare it with f(a). A failure at any step means f is not continuous at a.

concepts.name: Continuity of polynomials and rational functions
concepts.statement: Polynomials and rational functions are continuous at every point in their domains.

concepts.name: Removable discontinuity
concepts.statement: A function f discontinuous at a has a removable discontinuity at a if the limit of f(x) as x approaches a exists; its graph has a hole there.

concepts.name: Jump discontinuity
concepts.statement: A function f discontinuous at a has a jump discontinuity at a if the limits of f(x) from the left and from the right both exist as real numbers but are not equal.

concepts.name: Infinite discontinuity
concepts.statement: A function f discontinuous at a has an infinite discontinuity at a if its limit from the left or from the right is +∞ or −∞; it lies at a vertical asymptote.

concepts.name: Continuity from the right
concepts.statement: A function f(x) is continuous from the right at a if the limit of f(x) as x approaches a from the right is f(a).

concepts.name: Continuity from the left
concepts.statement: A function f(x) is continuous from the left at a if the limit of f(x) as x approaches a from the left is f(a).

concepts.name: Continuity over an interval
concepts.statement: A function is continuous over an open interval if it is continuous at every point in it, and over a closed interval [a, b] if it is continuous at every point of (a, b), continuous from the right at a and from the left at b; its graph can then be traced without lifting the pencil.

concepts.name: Composite function theorem
concepts.statement: If f(x) is continuous at L and the limit of g(x) as x approaches a is L, then the limit of f(g(x)) as x approaches a is f(L).

concepts.name: Continuity of trigonometric functions
concepts.statement: Trigonometric functions are continuous over their entire domains.

concepts.name: Intermediate Value Theorem
concepts.statement: Let f be continuous over a closed, bounded interval [a, b]. If z is any real number between f(a) and f(b), then there is a number c in [a, b] satisfying f(c) = z.

concepts.name: Epsilon-delta definition of the limit
concepts.statement: Let f(x) be defined for all x ≠ a over an open interval containing a, and let L be a real number. Then the limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L if, for every ε > 0, there exists a δ > 0 such that if 0 < |x − a| < δ, then |f(x) − L| < ε.

concepts.name: Proving a limit with epsilon and delta
concepts.statement: To prove that the limit of a specific f(x) as x approaches a is L: let ε > 0; choose δ, found algebraically or geometrically from |f(x) − L| < ε; assume 0 < |x − a| < δ; use it to show |f(x) − L| < ε; conclude that the limit is L.

concepts.name: Triangle inequality
concepts.statement: The triangle inequality states that if a and b are any real numbers, then |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|.

concepts.name: A limit that does not exist
concepts.statement: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a does not exist if for every real number L there exists ε > 0 so that for all δ > 0 there is an x satisfying 0 < |x − a| < δ with |f(x) − L| ≥ ε.

concepts.name: Epsilon-delta one-sided limits
concepts.statement: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a from the right is L if for every ε > 0 there exists δ > 0 such that 0 < x − a < δ implies |f(x) − L| < ε; from the left, −δ < x − a < 0 replaces 0 < x − a < δ.

concepts.name: Epsilon-delta infinite limits
concepts.statement: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is +∞ if for every M > 0 there exists δ > 0 such that 0 < |x − a| < δ implies f(x) > M, and −∞ if it implies f(x) < −M.
